summary: The prepared base already contains the GLM DSA, Quark MXFP4, topk=2048, Mega-MoE adapter, context-parallel, and MTP implementation surfaces added after the source issue opened. Component-level CPU and real gfx950 GPU checks passed, but the complete GLM-5.2-MXFP4 distributed serving contract could not be qualified with one visible GPU and no staged 744B-class checkpoint, so this is not reported as a complete fix.

tests.what_was_measured: 16 CPU contract tests covering FP8-to-MXFP4 conversion metadata, activation quantization handoff, the ROCm MQA logits chunking bound, and FlashInfer Mega-MoE adapter semantics.
23 real gfx950 JIT-kernel tests, including topk=2048 comparisons with independent torch.topk references for ragged, strided, duplicate-heavy, constant, negative, and mixed-length inputs.
Real gfx950 AITER FP8 MQA logits plus SGL top-k integration; one test and three decode/prefill subtests verified identical valid topk=2048 selections with and without invalid-tail initialization.

tests.command: huggingface_hub.hf_hub_download('amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4', 'config.json') followed by a JSON contract probe
tests.what_was_measured: Checkpoint metadata only: GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM, 1M maximum positions, index_topk=2048, 256 experts/8 active, and Quark grouped FP4 with E8M0 scales and explicit non-MXFP4 exclusions. No weights were downloaded.

gpu_execution_evidence: One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950, unique ID 0x91222c17f0f648d7) executed the fast-top-k and DSA MQA/top-k tests. Logs: raw/gpu-fast-topk.txt, raw/gpu-dsa-skip-logits.txt, and raw/intake.txt.
remaining_limitations: The amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 weights were not staged or loaded; no model semantic accuracy or HTTP serving result was produced.
The requested TP/EP=8 deployment and current TP=4 AMD recipe require more GPUs than the single assigned MI355X.
Mega-MoE collectives/symmetric buffers, context parallelism, 1M-token memory behavior, and EAGLE/MTP generation were not exercised end to end.
CUDA-only DeepGEMM behavior cannot be verified on this ROCm node; passing ROCm Quark/AITER component tests does not establish CUDA parity.
No native C++ source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
The private prototype referenced by the open upstream issue was unavailable, so exact parity with every unpublished optimization cannot be established.
